objective: Protect the multi-host controller inbound HTTP boundary by defaulting host publication to loopback, requiring an explicit private reverse-proxy trust configuration for non-local access, enforcing the trusted proxy socket-peer allow-list, bounding request bodies and concurrent requests, preserving the existing response limit and read-only API, and documenting TLS and authentication termination without changing public data contracts.
decision_supported: Can the controller read-only HTTP projection be deployed without accidental public exposure or unbounded inbound resource consumption while retaining deterministic health, readiness and data behavior?
acceptance: The Issue #66 change is evaluated relative to fixed base 2a8ee1593b000bad55140497572205b403674801 and changes only the approved paths.
The rendered controller Compose service publishes port 8080 on 127.0.0.1 by default instead of all host interfaces.

CONTROLLER_BIND_ADDRESS accepts only literal loopback, RFC1918 IPv4 or IPv6 unique-local addresses; hostnames, unspecified addresses, link-local addresses, multicast addresses, reserved addresses and public addresses fail closed before the Backend serves requests.
Loopback publication uses local trust mode by default and requires no non-local trust configuration.

A non-loopback private publication requires WORKBENCH_CONTROLLER_TRUST_MODE=reverse_proxy and a non-empty WORKBENCH_CONTROLLER_TRUSTED_PROXY_ALLOWLIST containing only literal loopback or private IP addresses and CIDR ranges.
Missing, blank, malformed or wildcard trusted-proxy configuration rejects non-loopback deployment before the Backend serves data.
In reverse-proxy mode, the Backend authorizes requests using the actual socket peer address; X-Forwarded-For, Forwarded and similar client-supplied headers never bypass the socket-peer allow-list.
An untrusted socket peer receives a bounded fail-closed response and cannot access static files, health, readiness, OpenAPI, run summaries or event data.

The existing healthz and readyz routes remain operational endpoints with bounded status-only responses, while API data remains under the existing read-only API routes; this Packet does not introduce a second listener or change OpenAPI response shapes.
GET and other bodyless read requests reject non-empty request bodies, transfer-encoded bodies, duplicate Content-Length values and malformed Content-Length values before routing.
Write requests with a body no larger than 1048576 bytes continue to return 405 read_only; a declared body larger than 1048576 bytes returns 413 without reading the complete body.
The server permits no more than 16 concurrently executing requests and rejects excess work with a bounded 503 server_busy response instead of creating unbounded request threads.
A complete encoded JSON response of 4194304 bytes remains permitted and a 4194305-byte response returns 413 response_too_large.
POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE continue to expose no robot, ROS, semantic-action or other control operation.

The deployment documentation requires non-local deployments to place the controller behind a reverse proxy that terminates TLS, performs authentication and limits the source network; examples contain no credentials or real secrets.
The container deployment test proves the default published HostIp is loopback, the operational readiness endpoint works, a data endpoint remains read-only and a write attempt returns 405.
Existing Issue #71 event-source egress URL validation, DNS pinning, redirect rejection, response bounds, timeout bounds and readiness behavior remain unchanged.

No interfaces, OpenAPI contracts, shared Pydantic contracts, event payloads, World Model behavior, Agent Runtime behavior, Dashboard code, Motion code, robot control, firmware, simulation, hardware, CI or safety configuration is modified.
evidence: At fixed base 2a8ee1593b000bad55140497572205b403674801, git show 2a8ee1593b000bad55140497572205b403674801:deploy/multi-host/compose.controller.yaml shows --host 0.0.0.0 and a published port without host_ip, demonstrating accidental all-interface exposure.
Before implementation, services/backend/workbench_backend/server.py constructs the standard ThreadingHTTPServer without an application concurrency bound.

From a temporary archive of fixed base 2a8ee1593b000bad55140497572205b403674801, python -m pytest tests/unit/test_multi_host.py tests/unit/test_dashboard_backend.py tests/unit/test_multi_host_deployment.py -v reports 40 passed and 1 Docker-image-dependent skipped test.
The pre-implementation loopback publication test fails because the rendered Compose port has no 127.0.0.1 HostIp.
The pre-implementation trust-policy tests fail because CONTROLLER_BIND_ADDRESS, WORKBENCH_CONTROLLER_TRUST_MODE and WORKBENCH_CONTROLLER_TRUSTED_PROXY_ALLOWLIST are not validated or enforced.
The pre-implementation concurrency test fails because excess requests are not rejected at a fixed limit.
Verbose policy tests list accepted loopback and private addresses and rejected public, wildcard, link-local, multicast, reserved, hostname, blank and malformed cases.
The spoofed-header test proves a disallowed socket peer remains denied even when Forwarded or X-Forwarded-For names an allowed address.
The request-boundary tests prove the exact 1048576-byte and 1048577-byte body cases and reject transfer encoding and ambiguous lengths.
The concurrency test uses deterministic synchronization to hold 16 requests and proves request 17 receives 503 without relying on public network access or arbitrary sleeps.
The response test proves the exact 4194304-byte success and 4194305-byte rejection boundary.
Rendered Compose JSON proves default HostIp is 127.0.0.1 and contains no 0.0.0.0 or wildcard host publication.
The dedicated Docker runtime smoke prints the inspected port binding and HTTP status evidence for readiness, read-only data access and rejected writes.
Documentation tests prove that reverse proxy, TLS, authentication, network allow-list, health/readiness exposure and secret-handling requirements are present.
Existing Issue #71 and Dashboard tests remain green.
Task Packet validation against 2a8ee1593b000bad55140497572205b403674801 proves every Git-visible change is within allowed_paths.
stop_conditions: The Integration/Deployment Owner does not approve changes to deploy/multi-host/compose.controller.yaml, docs/deployment/multi-host.md and the associated deployment tests.
The owning humans require health and readiness to use a physically separate listener or port instead of the approved route-level separation.
The owning humans require the Backend itself to terminate TLS, manage users, validate credentials, store secrets or implement an authentication protocol.
Docker networking prevents the Backend from observing a trustworthy socket peer and the proposed policy would have to trust client-supplied Forwarded or X-Forwarded-For values.
A public, unspecified, wildcard, link-local, multicast or reserved bind address must be accepted.
A non-loopback private bind can serve data without both reverse_proxy trust mode and a valid trusted-proxy allow-list.
The implementation requires changing docs/api-openapi-v1.json, the packaged OpenAPI document, interfaces, shared contracts or public response shapes.
The implementation requires changing services/backend/workbench_backend/remote_http.py, services/backend/workbench_backend/read_model.py or weakening any Issue #71 egress protection.

The implementation requires changes in World Model, Agent Runtime, Perception, Dashboard, Motion, robot control, firmware, simulation, hardware, deployment outside the controller Compose file, CI or safety configuration.
A deterministic concurrency bound cannot be enforced without leaking threads, sockets or request bodies.
The focused red tests fail before implementation for a reason other than the missing inbound bind, trust, request or concurrency policy.
The Docker runtime smoke cannot prove the effective HostIp and read-only HTTP behavior without relying on an external public network.
Unrelated user modifications overlap an allowed path.
Task Packet boundary validation reports any path outside allowed_paths.
data_classification: Repository-local synthetic HTTP requests, loopback/private test addresses and non-secret deployment fixtures only.
model_policy: Deterministic local Python, Docker Compose rendering and local container tests only; no model inference, public network calls, credentials or external authentication services.
risks_and_fallbacks: The fixed concurrency value of 16 is a proposed local controller policy, not an existing public contract; change it only before Packet approval.

This Packet interprets health/readiness separation as separate routes and exposure policy on the existing listener. If physical port separation is required, stop and create a separately reviewed design.
Reverse-proxy mode depends on the actual socket peer remaining visible through the chosen Docker networking topology; runtime evidence must verify this instead of assuming it.
The Backend does not terminate TLS or authenticate users. Non-local operation remains prohibited unless an external reverse proxy supplies TLS, authentication and network restriction.
Do not log trust credentials, authorization headers or complete untrusted request bodies.
Fail closed when address classification, proxy source identity, Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding or concurrency state is ambiguous.
If non-local deployment cannot be proven safe, fall back to the default loopback-only publication rather than widening exposure.

Rollback must revert the Backend inbound policy, server wiring, controller Compose configuration, documentation, tests, fixture and Task Packet together; the safe operational fallback is loopback-only access.
